persona: Terri Maxson balances a structured, community‑centric life with a lively social pulse, yet their tendency toward anxiety and occasional neglect of self‑care adds a touch of restless humanity to their otherwise orderly world.
cultural_background: Terri was raised in a middle-class, white, Midwestern family in the Detroit metropolitan area. Her upbringing reflects the values of hard work, punctuality, and neighborly care typical of suburban Michigan. She grew up in a Protestant (Methodist) household that emphasized community service, holiday traditions, and weekly family meals. The cultural fabric of Macomb County—shaped by automotive industry roots, strong labor unions, and seasonal celebrations—has reinforced her practical outlook and deep ties to local schools, churches, and neighborhood events.
skills_and_expertise: Terri possesses deep expertise in elementary and middle school instruction, including curriculum development aligned with Michigan state standards, differentiated instruction, classroom management, and parent-teacher communication. She is proficient with educational technology such as interactive whiteboards, Google Classroom, and assessment software. Her organizational strengths support effective lesson planning, data-driven instruction, and coordination of after-school programs. She also has experience in mentoring new teachers, conducting staff workshops, and leading school-wide literacy initiatives.
